description: Preserve the completed Markdown navigation work and add a small batch-seal path that finalizes many source runs against one immutable wiki snapshot.

userStories.title: Build deterministic Markdown structure nodes
userStories.description: As the bootstrap retrieval runtime, I need a deterministic heading-tree primitive so raw Markdown structure can be indexed without PageIndex or LLM dependencies.
acceptanceCriteria: A pure Python structure builder reuses the existing Markdown heading and byte-offset logic and ignores headings inside fenced code blocks.

Every Markdown document has a deterministic document root and deterministic heading nodes with node id, parent id, ordinal, depth, title, heading path, own line/byte range, and full subtree line/byte range.
Heading hierarchy uses ATX levels, preserves preamble and heading order, handles documents with no headings, and never drops nodes for thinning.
The same bytes and structure schema version produce byte-identical node records across repeated builds.
Focused structure tests pass without adding third-party dependencies.
userStories.notes: Keep this story to the pure structure builder and focused tests. Do not persist nodes or add CLI commands yet.

userStories.title: Persist and query raw Markdown structure
userStories.description: As a generated vault user, I need tree, ancestor, and subtree queries connected to raw FTS results so I can recover document context and reopen the exact canonical Markdown range.
acceptanceCriteria: The disposable raw SQLite schema is version-bumped and stores one raw_structure_nodes table plus raw_chunks.node_id; incompatible prior databases rebuild rather than migrate.
Incremental rebuild inserts, replaces, and deletes structure nodes with their owning document while preserving current raw FTS behavior and body-storage posture.
Search results add node_id without removing or changing existing result fields.
CLI commands tree <raw-path>, ancestors <node-id>, and subtree <node-id> return deterministic JSON; subtree reopens the current canonical raw byte range.
tree, ancestors, and subtree compare the indexed document checksum with current Markdown bytes and return state=stale plus rebuild guidance and no structure/content when they differ.
Read commands never rebuild implicitly; ordinary FTS search retains its current unchecked source_candidate/stale_candidate behavior and remains usable when structure lookup is stale.
Doctor validates node containment, parent references, chunk node references, and canonical hashes; focused raw retrieval tests pass.
userStories.notes: Do not add vectors, ranking fusion, a server, UI, PageIndex, or workflow hard gates.

userStories.title: Integrate optional structure navigation with the wiki loop
userStories.description: As an llm-wiki-loop operator, I need clear structure-first guidance so the loop can use heading context when helpful while canonical Markdown and the existing coverage receipt remain authoritative.
acceptanceCriteria: Generated SQLite-enabled vault instructions document raw tree, ancestors, and subtree as optional planning aids and explain explicit rebuild/stale behavior.

llm-wiki-loop instructs the semantic owner to use node paths or subtrees only when helpful, reopen canonical Markdown before synthesis, and fall back to direct Markdown reading when SQLite is off, unavailable, or stale.
Tree leaves are not declared source units, no tree coverage ledger is added, and wiki_workflow.py plus its completion gates remain unchanged.
Email, PDF, PageIndex runtime dependencies, JavaScript/TypeScript, UI, LLM node summaries, and automatic tree repair remain out of scope.
Affected current docs and wiki/_meta/log.md describe the new optional derived navigation boundary.
Focused tests, full unit tests, skill inventory validation, Repo Docs validation, and git diff checks pass with no errors or warnings.
userStories.notes: Documentation and integration only except for tests that enforce generated text. Never modify .agents/skills/llm-wiki-loop/scripts/wiki_workflow.py.

userStories.title: Seal a multi-source batch on one wiki snapshot
userStories.description: As a wiki batch operator, I need staged source work to be finalized together after one canonical apply so later sources do not make earlier source reviews stale before certification.
acceptanceCriteria: A batch seal operation accepts only a once-applied batch whose current corpus fingerprint still equals the writer result fingerprint.
Seal records every non-deferred linked source run's batch-applied mutation stages, structural validation, and ready final review against the same corpus snapshot without mutating wiki files.
Seal requires a bounded review receipt plus one valid applied full-coverage receipt per full-mode source and rejects missing, stale, incomplete, or mismatched evidence.

All sealed source runs reference the same batch corpus fingerprint while retaining their source-specific completion fingerprints, retrieval refresh runs at most once for the batch, and certification is written immediately from that snapshot.
Any canonical mutation after apply or after certification remains stale and blocking; single-source workflow freshness behavior is unchanged.
A two-source regression test proves one apply and one seal produce a passing certification, while focused and full quality gates pass.
userStories.notes: Keep the patch batch-specific. Do not weaken ordinary source-run freshness, exclude canonical wiki files from fingerprints, or introduce a second canonical ledger.
